groups.label: Verify one ABHA Number is linked to the unique patient ID in HIMS

rows.functionality: Verify one ABHA Number is linked to the unique patient ID in HIMS
rows.expected: HIMS is able to tag Patient ID with ABHA number.
rows.detail: Test: Intergrator's HIMS System should allow tagging of one ABHA Number with unique patient Id. Steps: ABHA Number should be validated in the database if already exists before creating a new patient id to avoid tagging of multiple patient id with same ABHA Number. Kindly Note: This test scenario is applicable for both new and existing beneficiaries and linking will be happens with ABHA creation and verification flow.

rows.expected: 1. Log into PHR app. 2. User will scan the QR code which is placed at the facility premises/registration desk. 3. Post scanning, patient profile details are displayed including ABHA number, ABHA address, Name, Gender, DoB, Mobile No and Address. Below this consent language is displayed - "Your consent to the above information to be shared with <HIP Name>. They can use this information for your registration and linking your health records" and both "Cancel" / "Share" buttons are provided. 4.Check that after clicking on "Share" button, user profile is successfully shared with the HIP and if user click on "Cancel" button then user profile is not shared with the HIP. 5. User clicks on share and gets a token number. 6. User clicks on ok and gets token number with validity of 30 minutes.
rows.detail: Test: User will scan the QR code which is placed the facility premises Steps: 1. Log into PHR app. 2. User will scan the QR code which is placed at the facility premises/registration desk. 3. Post scanning, patient profile details are displayed including ABHA number, ABHA address, Name, Gender, DoB, Mobile No and Address. Below this consent language is displayed - "Your consent to the above information to be shared with <HIP Name>. They can use this information for your registration and linking your health records" and both "Cancel" / "Share" buttons are provided. 4.Check that after clicking on "Share" button, user profile is successfully shared with the HIP and if user click on "Cancel" button then user profile is not shared with the HIP. 5. User clicks on share and gets a token number. 6. User clicks on ok and gets token number with validity of 30 minutes.

rows.expected: The person types the code and comes out with a 14 digit ABHA number.
rows.detail: Not an NHA test case. It sat under 'ABHA creation, Aadhaar OTP'. Send the txnId and the encrypted OTP. Success is HTTP 200 carrying ABHAProfile.ABHANumber, tokens.token and tokens.refreshToken. The number matches 91-\d{4}-\d{4}-\d{4} and passes the Luhn checksum on its 14 digits. A 400 whose body key is txnId means the wrong transaction id. A 422 with ABDM-1204 means Aadhaar rejected the attempt, and the UIDAI code inside the message says why.

rows.expected: A wrong code fails cleanly and creates nothing.
rows.detail: Not an NHA test case. It sat under 'ABHA creation, Aadhaar OTP'. Repeat the OTP request, then send a deliberately wrong encrypted OTP. Success is a non 200 with no ABHAProfile.ABHANumber in the body. The exact code for a wrong Aadhaar OTP is not transcribed in either source, so assert on the absence of the field and on the status, not on a code. Check your own database too: a failed enrolment must leave no partial patient record.

rows.expected: A finished attempt cannot be replayed to create a second ABHA.
rows.detail: Not an NHA test case. It sat under 'ABHA creation, Aadhaar OTP'. Take a txnId from a completed enrolment and send it again. Success is HTTP 400 with a body key of txnId and the value Invalid Transaction Id, or an equivalent rejection. HTTP 200 and a second ABHA number is a failure.

rows.expected: The number the person named is now on their profile.
rows.detail: Not an NHA test case. It sat under 'ABHA creation, Aadhaar OTP'. Send the same scope and the encrypted OTP. Success is HTTP 200 here and a profile readback whose mobile equals the number you sent. A profile whose mobile is still the Aadhaar linked number is a failure.

rows.functionality: Keep the two OTP systems apart
rows.expected: A code from NHA is refused at the Aadhaar endpoint.
rows.detail: Not an NHA test case. It sat under 'ABHA creation, Aadhaar OTP'. Take a valid mobile OTP obtained with otpSystem "abdm" and send it to enrol by Aadhaar instead of to auth/byAbdm. Success is a non 200, proving your routing is by scope. HTTP 200 means something sends both codes to the same endpoint. Sandbox lets that pass. Production will not.

rows.functionality: Accept a non Aadhaar mobile number
rows.expected: A family phone or a changed number works as the communication number.
rows.detail: Not an NHA test case. It sat under 'ABHA creation, Aadhaar OTP'. Run the mobile request and verify pair with a number different from the one the Aadhaar OTP went to. Success is HTTP 200 on both calls and a profile whose mobile is the new number. A rejection naming loginId points at your encryption, not at the number.

rows.expected: The address the person chose is the address they end up with.
rows.detail: Not an NHA test case. It sat under 'ABHA creation, Aadhaar OTP'. Send the chosen address with preferred: 1. Success is HTTP 200 with healthIdNumber in the body, and a later profile read whose preferredAbhaAddress starts with the address you sent. A different address, or an auto generated one built from the ABHA number, is a failure. Enrolment ends here.

rows.expected: An Aadhaar registered device produces a signed capture of the person's fingerprint or iris.
rows.detail: Not an NHA test case. It sat under 'ABHA creation, Aadhaar biometric'. The device encrypts and digitally signs the PID block. UIDAI publishes the approved devices at uidai.gov.in. NHA's M1 document shows this step only as screenshots, so the fields are not transcribed.

rows.functionality: Create the ABHA from the scan
rows.expected: The person gets a 14 digit ABHA number without typing a code.
rows.detail: Not an NHA test case. It sat under 'ABHA creation, Aadhaar biometric'. Fingerprint and iris are two flows in NHA's document and both run against this call with the signed data block and the Aadhaar details. The request body is not transcribed. After enrolment this route continues with the same mobile, optional email, address and link steps as the Aadhaar OTP route.

rows.expected: The portal shows a QR code for the person to scan with the ABHA app.
rows.detail: Not an NHA test case. It sat under 'ABHA creation, Aadhaar biometric'. Send scope ["abha-enrol","face-auth"]. Turn the returned txnId into a QR code and show it. The person opens the ABHA app, taps Portal Face Auth, scans the code, and completes face authentication through the Aadhaar registered device service. Plan the screen that tells them to install the app first.

rows.expected: The portal waits until the person has finished on their phone, then moves on.
rows.detail: Not an NHA test case. It sat under 'ABHA creation, Aadhaar biometric'. This call answers HTTP 200 every time, so branch on status: PENDING, then VERIFIED, then COMPLETE. Stop at COMPLETE. Your system drives this loop. M1 has no callbacks and NHA never calls you.

rows.functionality: Create the ABHA from the face
rows.expected: The person gets a 14 digit ABHA number after face authentication.
rows.detail: Not an NHA test case. It sat under 'ABHA creation, Aadhaar biometric'. Send authMethods ["face_auth"] with the transaction id, then continue at the communication mobile step of the Aadhaar OTP route.

rows.expected: The person gets a 14 digit ABHA number with no code and no scan.
rows.detail: Not an NHA test case. It sat under 'ABHA creation, demographic authentication'. One call, with authMethods ["demo_auth"] and a demo_auth object holding the encrypted Aadhaar number, name, date of birth, gender, state code and district code, plus a consent block of code abha-enrollment and version 1.4. Mobile, address, profile photo, pincode and consentHealthId are optional in that object. NHA marks this route mandatory for government integrators and not required for private ones.

rows.expected: The children mapped to a parent's ABHA number come back.
rows.detail: Not an NHA test case. It sat under 'ABHA creation, demographic authentication'. A child ABHA is issued for a child under six with no Aadhaar number, on the consent of a parent or guardian, and it links to the parent's ABHA number. NHA reaches it through government health programmes and restricts it to government integrators by leadership approval. Skip it unless NHA has enabled it for you.

rows.expected: A code reaches the mobile number the person gave.
rows.detail: Not an NHA test case. It sat under 'ABHA creation, driving licence or PAN'. Send scope ["abha-enrol","mobile-verify","dl-flow"], loginHint "mobile", otpSystem "abdm" and the encrypted mobile number. The third scope value is what marks this as the document route.

rows.expected: The mobile number is confirmed before the document goes anywhere.
rows.detail: Not an NHA test case. It sat under 'ABHA creation, driving licence or PAN'. Send the same three scope values, authMethods ["otp"], the txnId from the request and the encrypted OTP.

rows.functionality: Create the ABHA from the document
rows.expected: The person gets an ABHA number from an identity document instead of Aadhaar.
rows.detail: Not an NHA test case. It sat under 'ABHA creation, driving licence or PAN'. The body carries txnId, documentType, documentId, the name parts, dob, gender, front and back photos, address, state, district, pinCode and a consent block. NHA's collection uses a driving licence. The account created this way is restricted until it is upgraded through Aadhaar KYC, so tell the person that rather than letting them discover it later.

rows.functionality: Request a login OTP from Aadhaar
rows.expected: A code reaches the mobile number linked to the person's Aadhaar.
rows.detail: Not an NHA test case. It sat under 'ABHA verification, Aadhaar OTP'. For a person who typed their 14 digit ABHA number, send loginHint "abha-number", scope ["abha-login","aadhaar-verify"] and otpSystem "aadhaar". Keep the txnId.

rows.expected: A person who knows their 14 digit number is signed in.
rows.detail: Not an NHA test case. It sat under 'ABHA verification, Aadhaar OTP'. Run it twice: once with scope ["abha-login","aadhaar-verify"] and otpSystem "aadhaar", once with scope ["abha-login","mobile-verify"] and otpSystem "abdm". Both runs pass with HTTP 200, authResult of success, and a non empty token, refreshToken and numeric expiresIn. A 400 naming scope means the scope values differ between the request and the verify call. They must be identical.

rows.expected: A person who typed their Aadhaar number gets a code.
rows.detail: Not an NHA test case. It sat under 'ABHA verification, Aadhaar OTP'. Send scope ["abha-login","aadhaar-verify","aadhaar-otp-verify"], loginHint "aadhaar" and otpSystem "aadhaar". This route sits on the v3.1 base URL at https://abhasbx.abdm.gov.in/abha/api/v3.1/. The rest of M1 is on v3.

rows.expected: The person is signed in with their Aadhaar number.
rows.detail: Not an NHA test case. It sat under 'ABHA verification, Aadhaar OTP'. Send the same three scope values as the request, the txnId and the encrypted OTP. You receive token, refreshToken and expiresIn.

rows.functionality: Request a login OTP by mobile
rows.expected: A code reaches the person, and the screen names the masked number it went to.
rows.detail: Not an NHA test case. It sat under 'ABHA verification, mobile OTP'. Send scope ["abha-login","mobile-verify"], loginHint "mobile" and otpSystem "abdm". Success is HTTP 200 with a txnId and a message naming the masked mobile. Show that message to the person.

rows.expected: The code is accepted and the accounts on that number are offered.
rows.detail: Not an NHA test case. It sat under 'ABHA verification, mobile OTP'. Send the txnId and the encrypted OTP. Success is HTTP 200. One mobile number can hold several ABHA accounts, so a third call follows.

rows.functionality: Pick an account and sign in
rows.expected: The person picks their ABHA from the list and is logged in.
rows.detail: Not an NHA test case. It sat under 'ABHA verification, mobile OTP'. Send the ABHA number the person picked, with the transaction token in the T-token header. Success is HTTP 200 with token and refreshToken in the body. A 400 here usually means T-token is missing. It is the only M1 call that uses that header. The collection has no shortcut for a number with exactly one ABHA behind it, so build all three calls.

rows.expected: A wrong code does not log anybody in.
rows.detail: Not an NHA test case. It sat under 'ABHA verification, mobile OTP'. Request a login OTP, then verify with a wrong encrypted OTP. Success is a non 200 with no token in the body. HTTP 200, or any token present, is a failure. Check your session store holds nothing for that person afterwards.

rows.expected: A person who knows their 14 digit number signs in with a code from NHA.
rows.detail: Not an NHA test case. It sat under 'ABHA verification, mobile OTP'. Two calls, the same pair as the Aadhaar route with loginHint "abha-number", scope ["abha-login","mobile-verify"] and otpSystem "abdm". There is also a password route: one call to verify a login with scope ["abha-login","password-verify"] and an authData.password object holding the ABHA number and the encrypted password. No OTP request comes first.

rows.expected: The portal shows a QR code for the person to scan with the ABHA app.
rows.detail: Not an NHA test case. It sat under 'ABHA verification, biometric'. NHA's collection reuses the enrolment auth init call to get the txnId that the login QR code is built from.

rows.expected: The person is signed in after face authentication.
rows.detail: Not an NHA test case. It sat under 'ABHA verification, biometric'. This verify sits on the v3.1 base URL, not v3. NHA's collection has a variant that carries the PID block and one that does not.

rows.functionality: Sign in by fingerprint or iris
rows.expected: The person is signed in with a scan from an Aadhaar registered device.
rows.detail: Not an NHA test case. It sat under 'ABHA verification, biometric'. Fingerprint and iris are separate requests in NHA's collection against the same v3.1 verify call. NHA's M1 document shows the request bodies only as screenshots, so the fields are not transcribed. Write the checks from what you observe against sandbox.

rows.expected: The mobile number leaves your system scrambled.
rows.detail: Not an NHA test case. It sat under 'Fetch ABHA by mobile number'. Post the plain value and use the encryptedData that comes back. This is what NHA's collection does for the find ABHA flow. The other option is to fetch NHA's public certificate and encrypt locally, better for production because the plain value never leaves your system.

rows.expected: The ABHA accounts held against that mobile number come back.
rows.detail: Not an NHA test case. It sat under 'Fetch ABHA by mobile number'. Send scope ["search-abha"] and the encrypted mobile. Keep the transaction id. The two pieces of evidence in NHA's collection disagree on the response shape, so confirm it against sandbox before you rely on it.

rows.expected: A code reaches the person for the account they chose.
rows.detail: Not an NHA test case. It sat under 'Fetch ABHA by mobile number'. Send scope ["abha-login","search-abha","mobile-verify"], loginHint "index", and the search transaction id in txnId.

rows.functionality: Verify the OTP and sign in
rows.expected: The person is signed in to the ABHA they picked.
rows.detail: Not an NHA test case. It sat under 'Fetch ABHA by mobile number'. Send scope ["abha-login","mobile-verify"] with the encrypted OTP. You receive the user token.

rows.functionality: Find the ABHA behind an Aadhaar
rows.expected: The ABHA number recorded against that Aadhaar number comes back.
rows.detail: Not an NHA test case. It sat under 'Fetch ABHA by Aadhaar number'. A benefit scheme lookup, not a general search. The Aadhaar value is encrypted. NHA restricts the benefit endpoints to government integrators.

rows.functionality: Find the Aadhaar behind an ABHA
rows.expected: The Aadhaar number recorded against that ABHA number comes back.
rows.detail: Not an NHA test case. It sat under 'Fetch ABHA by Aadhaar number'. The other half of the same pair in NHA's collection, under the same government only restriction.

rows.expected: A private integrator is turned away from the benefit endpoints.
rows.detail: Not an NHA test case. It sat under 'Fetch ABHA by Aadhaar number'. As a private integrator, call any profile/benefit/ endpoint. Expect HTTP 401 with ABDM-1094. The result is quoted from a saved example in NHA's collection.

rows.expected: The person sees the QR code that shares their ABHA at a facility desk.
rows.detail: Not an NHA test case. It sat under 'ABHA QR code'. Gateway token in Authorization, user token in X-token, the same two headers as the profile call. The response shape is not transcribed, because NHA's document shows it as a screenshot.

rows.expected: The person sees their ABHA card.
rows.detail: Not an NHA test case. It sat under 'ABHA QR code'. Same two headers. NHA shows the card arriving inside the response rather than as a URL to fetch, and the response shape is not transcribed.

rows.expected: The person can save their ABHA card as a file.
rows.detail: Not an NHA test case. It sat under 'ABHA QR code'. Same two headers. The response shape is not transcribed.

rows.functionality: Check the card and code render
rows.expected: The card and the QR code both come back and can be shown to the person.
rows.detail: Not an NHA test case. It sat under 'ABHA QR code'. Call all three of the above. Success is HTTP 200 from each with a non empty body. Any non 200 is a failure. Because the response shapes are not transcribed in either source, assert on the status and a non empty body, then record what you actually received.

rows.expected: A code reaches the number the person wants to move to.
rows.detail: Not an NHA test case. It sat under 'Profile update'. Send scope ["abha-profile","mobile-verify"] and the new number, encrypted. Both the gateway token and the user token are needed. Success is HTTP 200 with a txnId.

rows.expected: The new number shows on the person's profile.
rows.detail: Not an NHA test case. It sat under 'Profile update'. Send the same scope and the encrypted OTP. Success is HTTP 200 followed by a profile read showing the new mobile. A 400 with {"message": "Invalid X-token"} means you sent the gateway token where the user token belongs. Both headers are needed here. The verify response body is not transcribed, so assert on the status and the readback, not on a field in the response.

rows.expected: The same pair of calls covers the other profile changes.
rows.detail: Not an NHA test case. It sat under 'Profile update'. The email update, password change, re-KYC, delete and deactivate flows use the same request and verify pair with a different second scope value. NHA marks re-KYC optional for private and government integrators alike.

rows.expected: The person's self declared details change on their profile.
rows.detail: Not an NHA test case. It sat under 'Profile update'. Changing a mobile number or an email address is not done here. Those need the OTP pair above, because NHA verifies the new value before accepting it. NHA's collection uses this call to change the profile photo.

rows.expected: The profile shows the ABHA number, address and mobile the person created.
rows.detail: Not an NHA test case. It sat under 'Share patient profile'. Gateway token in Authorization, user token in X-token, both required. Success is HTTP 200 with ABHANumber, preferredAbhaAddress and mobile matching what was created, and non empty name, gender and the three date of birth fields. An ABHA number that is not the one you logged in as means the user token belongs to a different session, so check you are not reusing a token across test runs. The field list comes from a saved example on the PATCH of the same path, not on the GET.

rows.expected: The profile comes back only when your system and the person both prove themselves.
rows.detail: Not an NHA test case. It sat under 'Share patient profile'. Call it three times: with both headers, with Authorization only, and with X-token only. Success is HTTP 200 with both and a non 200 for each of the other two. If X-token alone works, your gateway token is being read from somewhere else, such as a proxy that injects it.

rows.functionality: Share the profile at the desk
rows.expected: The person shares their ABHA address and profile with the facility after consenting.
rows.detail: Not an NHA test case. It sat under 'Share patient profile'. NHA puts this outside the M1 API set. The facility shows a QR code carrying a hip-id and a counter-id. The person scans it with a PHR app, the app shows everything that will be shared and takes consent in NHA's wording, and only then calls the HIE-CM to share the details. The facility can return a token number. NHA's PHR app test pack marks the scan and share steps mandatory.

rows.expected: Your system can prove who it is to NHA.
rows.detail: Not an NHA test case. It sat under 'Session and tokens'. Send your sandbox client id and secret with grantType "client_credentials". Success is HTTP 200 with a non empty accessToken. Every later call carries it in the Authorization header. A 401 with {"code": "900901"} means the credentials are wrong, not the request. Check the X-CM-ID: sbx header, which the sessions call needs and no other M1 call has.

rows.expected: The Aadhaar number, mobile number and code that leave your system are scrambled, not readable.
rows.detail: Not an NHA test case. It sat under 'Session and tokens'. Encrypt every Aadhaar number, mobile number, email address, OTP value and password before you send it. Success is HTTP 200 with encryptedData present, not equal to the input, and longer than it. Also a failure: any place in your own code where a plain Aadhaar number, mobile number or OTP reaches a request body. Grep for it.

rows.functionality: Reject a call with no token
rows.expected: A call that carries no token is refused.
rows.detail: Not an NHA test case. It sat under 'Session and tokens'. Call the profile with the Authorization header removed. Success is HTTP 401 with a code of 900901 or an error.code. HTTP 200 means something other than NHA is answering you, most likely a cached response. Stop and find out what.

rows.expected: A session longer than half an hour keeps working without showing the person an error.
rows.detail: Not an NHA test case. It sat under 'Session and tokens'. The one saved login example gives the user token an expiresIn of 1800 seconds. Wait past it and a profile call returns a non 200, one shape being a 400 with {"message": "Invalid X-token"}. Put the refresh token in the R-token header, not X-token and not the body. Success is HTTP 200 with a new token and refreshToken, and a profile call that then succeeds. Store the new refresh token and treat the old one as spent. Neither source says whether the old one keeps working.

rows.expected: When the person logs out, their token stops working.
rows.detail: Not an NHA test case. It sat under 'Session and tokens'. Success is HTTP 200 with {"message": "You have been logged out"}, then a non 200 from a profile call made with the same user token. A profile call that still returns HTTP 200 and profile data is a failure.

rows.expected: A wrong URL gives a clear not found.
rows.detail: Not an NHA test case. It sat under 'Session and tokens'. Call profile/lo/verify instead of profile/login/verify. Expect HTTP 404 with "No matching resource found for given API Request".

rows.expected: An empty request names the fields it wanted.
rows.detail: Not an NHA test case. It sat under 'Session and tokens'. POST an empty body to verify a login. Expect HTTP 400 with both scope and authData as keys in the response.

rows.expected: A broken Authorization value is refused.
rows.detail: Not an NHA test case. It sat under 'Session and tokens'. Send a malformed Authorization value to any M1 call. Expect HTTP 401 with a code of 900901.

rows.expected: A 13 digit ABHA number is refused.
rows.detail: Not an NHA test case. It sat under 'Session and tokens'. Send a 13 digit ABHA number to any endpoint that takes one. Expect HTTP 400 with ABDM-1013, Invalid ABHA Number.
